claim.quote: In this contribution we report the first observation of dilepton emission from QCD matter at high net-baryon density

key_value_text.quote: the average temperature of the radiating fireball formed in Au+Au collision at √ sN N = 2.42 GeV was found to be 71.8 ± 2.1 MeV
key_value_text.value: average temperature of the radiating fireball in Au+Au at sqrt(sNN) = 2.42 GeV: 71.8 ± 2.1 MeV

name: HADES first observation of dilepton emission from baryon-rich QCD matter
notes: The claim is the paper's own wording ("we report the first observation of dilepton emission from QCD matter at high net-baryon density"), taken from the repository copy of the published paper (the arXiv version was not located).

summary.plain: HADES recorded the electron-positron pairs radiated by the hot, dense fireball in gold-gold collisions, and reports the first observation of dilepton emission from QCD matter at high net-baryon density, like the matter in neutron-star mergers. The fireball temperature came out at about 72 MeV.
summary.technical: Dielectron emission from Au+Au collisions at sqrt(sNN) = 2.42 GeV: after subtraction of the contribution from hadron decays the excess is thermal-like radiation; the average temperature of the radiating fireball is 71.8 ± 2.1 MeV with densities up to three times normal nuclear density, with an in-medium rho spectral function strongly broadened by baryons.

title: Probing dense baryon-rich matter with virtual photons
why_it_matters: Dilepton thermometry of matter at high net-baryon density complements the NA60 and CERES measurements at high energy and supports the equation-of-state studies of neutron-star mergers.
